  stdout is not a terminal; what `list --json` gains is a fork for the operator (the directive's item 3).
- **A reused name never inherits an old parent** — a parent belongs to one instance's launch, not to its name.
- **Parent kept by `revive`** — a revived instance keeps the parent its lineage recorded.
- **A parent edge is a drawing label only** — it never changes the wheel, the links or whether a `send` is accepted.

body: M1 — **the test run under the fake agent.** `cargo test --features fake-agent --test cli_list --test cli_links --test cli_revive --test cli_output_plain --test chaos_revive -- --test-threads 4` at f274938f: exit 0; `cli_list` 21 passed, `cli_links` 12, `cli_revive` 27, `cli_output_plain` 6, `chaos_revive` 1 — 67 passed, 0 failed (log: `$TMPDIR/{scratchpad}/p3-measure-1.log`, the five `test result:` lines read from it).

M2 — **the parent/child relation the tree holds today: none.** No event kind, snapshot field, board field or flag names a parent or a role: `viola_core::EventKind` holds 15 kinds (`crates/viola-core/src/lib.rs:58-94`, `ALL: [Self; 15]`), none of them a lineage kind; `InstanceSnapshot` holds `endpoint, pid, started_at, pinned_bin, cli_verified, cli_version, wheel, links, child_pid, pending_dialog, cwd, agent_session_id` (`src/run/mod.rs:29-44`, the test literal); `RunArgs` takes `name` and `program` only (`src/cmd/run.rs:43-50`); `ReviveArgs` takes `name, --id, --fork, --list, --json, extra` (`src/cmd/revive.rs:25-44`). A search of all seven masters for `lineage|\bparent\b` (`rec.py find --doc {each} --regex '(?i)lineage|\bparent\b'`) finds 0 lineage rows; its 16 hits are other senses of «parent» (the R8 parent-identity env floor, a parent directory, a parent-death kill).

M3 — **the one relation it does hold: observed links.** `driver -> driven` pairs, written only by the driven wrapper as `link` / `unlink` lines (`source: wrapper`, `{driver, driven}`), held in memory by `LinkSet` (`src/run/links.rs:21-137`), mirrored to `snapshot.json`'s `links` at each change (`links.rs:130-136`), rebuilt by the replay's one rule `replay::apply_link_line`, restored at EVERY start, `run` and `revive` alike, before the endpoint serves (`src/cmd/run.rs:338-343`). The driver is self-reported (`from`, or the `link` verb's argument) and need not be a booted instance.

M4 — **a reused name inherits its links today.** `links_survive_a_wrapper_restart` (`tests/cli_links.rs:224-256`, in M1's green run) boots a second `viola run` of the same name over the first life's log and asserts the snapshot's `links` equal the first life's. A `run` of a `gone` name is taken over in place (`collision_check`, `src/cmd/run.rs:461-488`: `Gone` → `None`), its `events.ndjson` appended to, never truncated. So a parent derived from the log by the link rule would ALSO be inherited by a reused name — the requirement's «a reused name never inherits an old parent» needs its own rule (see Mechanism).

M5 — **what `revive` keeps today.** `revive` runs `run`'s own `start` (`src/cmd/revive.rs:152-156` → `src/cmd/run.rs:264`) after its preflight; it keeps the instance's log (appended), its link set (restored by the shared start), the session it resumes (`session_chain` → `pick_session`, `revive.rs:218-253`) and the recorded `cwd` (only from a real snapshot, `recorded_dir`, `revive.rs:257-266`). It keeps no parent (none exists, M2).
M7 — **what a launch knows of its parent at the moment it starts.**

- Environment NAMES a `viola run` inherits when typed inside a wrapped session: `VIOLA_NAME`, `VIOLA_DIR`, `VIOLA_BIN` — set by that session's wrapper on its `claude` child (`run::child_launch`, `src/run/mod.rs:138-143`) and inherited by whatever the child starts; they are not `CLAUDE*`, so the R8 strip never touches them. `viola run` reads two of them today, only to resolve its HOME (`resolved_home` → `instance_of`, `src/cmd/mod.rs:255-300`: the pair must check as `<home>/instances/<name>`); it never reads `VIOLA_NAME` as its own name (obs-plan · decision/instance-source-per-role). Its own child gets ITS name over the inherited one (`child_launch` sets `VIOLA_NAME` last-writer).
- The socket: the parent's endpoint is recorded in the parent's `snapshot.json`; a start reads no other instance's snapshot today.
- The record: none — no file names the caller.

- What it CANNOT know: whether the inherited `VIOLA_NAME` is honest (self-reported, as `from` is: security-plan · decision/from-field-authenticates-nothing); whether the parent is live (unless it reads the parent's snapshot and liveness, which it does not); anything at all when typed in a plain shell or by a human outside a wrapped session (no `VIOLA_NAME`); the parent's session id or socket (only through the parent's state files).

M8 — **where a start's own lines land.** `start_state` appends one `wheel {holder:"driver", cause:"start"}` line after the first snapshot and the heartbeat, before the spawn (`src/cmd/run.rs:559-591`); the hook's `session-start` follows from the child. test-plan · contract/boot-readiness/events and contract/event-log/start-wheel-record pin «line 1 `wheel` start, line 2 `session-start`» for a booted instance; decision/start-lines-read-from-start-offset reads a start's lines from its own offset.

## 2026-11-22-lineage-registry — 4. ARIA Patterns & Roles: 1 row(s)
**Section:** 4. ARIA Patterns & Roles
**Change:** ~ decision/cli-structural-landmark-equivalents · rule: was «The CLI has no landmark roles; its structure is carried by the BAY context line, the uppercase caption line, the `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` separator and the `--help` group labels.»; now «The CLI has no landmark roles; its structure is carried by the BAY context line, the uppercase caption line, the `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` separator, the `-- LINKS --` separator, the plain-space NAME indent of tree depth and the `--help` group labels.»
**Why:** decision/cli-structural-landmark-equivalents: The board gains a `-- LINKS --` separator and a NAME indent for tree depth as structure carriers, so the list of landmark equivalents is incomplete without them. — on relayed verbatim by overseer, 2026-11-22, inputs#I2 (F4, F5)
**Ref:** .andromeda/runs/2026-11-23T05-33-20Z-wrap/

- **P6 — CLI board, wait/last, verify** — cli output discipline; `viola list`'s `CAPTION` literal pins the caption order, which the terminal fleet console (matrix#v2-14) reuses; the wrapped rows are drawn as a tree, their depth carried by a plain-space NAME indent; the `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` separator stands too, printed only when unwrapped rows exist, and the links follow behind their `-- LINKS --` separator (the `--help` group labels stand too: board / traffic / wheel / handoff / setup over the served verbs, the `handoff:` row `handoff:  link, unlink` between `wheel:` and `setup:`, `plugin install` built in `setup:` as one entry and a bare `plugin` unserved)

- Arguments mirror channel params: `viola send <target>` (text from stdin or `--file`), `viola wait <target> [--after <cursor>] [--timeout-ms <n>]`, `viola last <target>`, `viola answer <target> <dialog_id>` (response JSON from stdin/`--file`), `viola pause <target>`, `viola release <target>` (a `--budget` flag is a usage error, exit 2), `viola link|unlink <driver> <driven>`; `viola revive <name> [--id <ID>] [--fork] [-- <child args>]` and `viola revive <name> --list` send no channel frame; `viola run --parent <NAME>` declares the instance's parent (one equal to its own name a usage error, exit 2, before anything is read; with no `--parent` an inherited `VIOLA_NAME` is taken as parent only, dropped when it equals the own name) and `viola run --role <WORD>` its role, a code word.

- Readers: over-long lines (> `MAX_FRAME`) count as `torn_lines`; unknown kinds/fields are counted in `skipped`; a reader never writes (the next append heals a torn last line). A snapshot with an unsupported `v` or a parse failure → replay (`state-recovered`) through `replay::read_snapshot_or_replay`, whose five product callers are `viola revive`'s preflight, `viola list`'s `board::read`, `liveness::live_endpoint`, `viola hook`'s `connect` (a replayed or absent snapshot unreachable, so the hook fails open) and `run`'s collision check (a replayed snapshot judged by the heartbeat alone); the replay writes no file, rebuilds `lineage` from the log (the last `lineage` line replacing the held value) and recovers `links` from the logged `link` / `unlink` lines through the public rule `replay::apply_link_line` (a pair keeps its first `since` until an `unlink`; a `link` line with no string `ts` reads `since: "unknown"`), which the root bin's `LinkSet` applies as well.

- Only the instance's wrapper writes its snapshot; only `viola verify` writes stamps; no process writes or reads a `budget.json` (no budget reading is kept). The board read model is `board.rs` (`scan` checks the home by the read rule (`check_read`, on Linux, with or without an instance, a refusal `ScanRefused::Home`), `instances/` by `check_path` and each instance without following a link; `read` gives one `Item` per live or stale instance, takes the replay for an unreadable or newer snapshot, and sums the skip counts of one `read_from` pass per instance; the agents join (`JoinKeys`, `Observation`, `join`, `Item::unwrapped`) folds one `claude agents --json` reading in: a row matching a wrapped item's `child_pid` or `agent_session_id` sets that item's `status` to `idle` or `busy`, and every unjoined row is an unwrapped item; no type holds `endpoint`, `pinned_bin`, `cwd`, `pid` or `started_at`). The snapshot holds no budget field (`budget_paused` and `budget_override_until` are gone; `v` stays 1). The snapshot holds no `statusline_command`; `SnapshotRead::Present` and `replay::Recovered::Snapshot` hold a `Box<InstanceSnapshot>`.

- `run` start order (before the wrapper log opens, every start, `run`'s and a revived one, checks the home tree: `checked_exe` reads the exe's bytes once and takes their pin key, then `viola_state::strict::check_home_tree` checks the home, the instance's set, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`, `bin/<key>/`, the pinned copy, `plugin/<key>/` and its `hooks/` and `.claude-plugin/`, each that exists — a refusal is exit 1 with the home pair, or the instance pair for an instance-level refusal, no log opened, no line and no child —, and the pin step pins those same bytes through `pin_bytes`; the home is canonicalised by `canonical_home` once the wrapper log has created it, before the collision check, the pin and the endpoint bind): program resolution (a given path as given, a bare name on `PATH`; it writes nothing) → collision check → pinned copy (placed once when absent, with no clobber, through `place_private_new`, and never replaced; SHA-256 re-hash on reuse and of a copy a concurrent first start placed first; a mismatch → exit 1 `pinned-hash-mismatch`, the file left as found) + plugin folder rewrite → strip plan → version gate (`run::version_gate`: `--version` with no user args, killed at 5 s, logged as a `version-probe` start/exit pair; the stamps read; `cli_version` / `cli_verified` (the start's final verdict: the gate's, its stamps read again after an automatic verify where one ran) into the first snapshot and the `claude-child` `process-start`; nothing printed) → `socket_dir_ready` (`src/cmd/run.rs`: `check_endpoint_dir`, create the parent only when absent, check again; a refused or uncreatable directory → exit 1 `socket-dir-refused`, left as found, before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`, the `unable:` / `hint:` pair and one `process-exit`; a `Server::bind` failure does not read this code) → exclusive endpoint bind (taken → exit 1 `squatted-name`) → any automatic verify (with `config.json`'s `verify_new_cli` on, default off, and no attempted stamps entry for the claude version: `viola verify` run once as a child, the home passed to it only through `--home`, only while holding the owner-only `ledger/verify.lock`, try-locked after the stamps strict-modes check and never the stamps lock, a held lock meaning no verify and an unverified start; an entry already attempted, a red one included, never verified again automatically; the start gating on the final verdict) → on a verified verdict, the trust record of an untrusted spawn folder written into the child's Claude config (located through `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` only when `claude_env_keep` keeps it) → first snapshot (with `endpoint`, and `lineage` `{parent?, role?}` from `--parent` / `--role`, with no `--parent` an inherited `VIOLA_NAME` other than the own name taken as parent) + heartbeat → `wheel` event → child spawn (R8 strip, `VIOLA_NAME` / `VIOLA_DIR` / `VIOLA_BIN`, pinned folder first on PATH, `--plugin-dir`) → snapshot rewritten with `child_pid`. A live holder or a fresh replayed beat → exit 1 `already-live`, a `stale` holder → exit 1 `stale-heartbeat` (the `run.collision_check` span's `outcome` reads `already-live` for both); a `gone` one is taken over at once. The collision check takes its caller's one snapshot read (`replay::read_snapshot_or_replay`): over a replayed snapshot, which holds no `pid` or `started_at`, it decides from the heartbeat alone, a beat at most `STALE_AFTER` old refusing `already-live` and an older one free; a failed read or no snapshot is free. The first snapshot records the spawn directory as `cwd` when it is valid UTF-8.

- `revive` (`src/cmd/revive.rs`) resumes a `gone` instance through the same `start`: first the strict-modes check (`trusted`: `check_instance` before the wrapper log opens; a refusal is the state-files pair and exit 1 with no log opened and no line), on the start arm then the home-tree check (`checked_exe`, then `refuse_tree`: the home, the instance's `check_instance` set, `ledger/`, `bin/`, `plugin/`, and for the running binary's pin key `bin/<key>/`, the pinned `viola`, `plugin/<key>/` and its `hooks/` and `.claude-plugin/`, each that exists; a refusal prints the home-state pair, or the instance-state pair when the refused path is the instance's, opens no log, writes no line and starts no child, and under `--json` is the `strict-modes-failed` document), then a preflight of four readings in a fixed order, stopping at the first refusal (`session-live` is one `claude agents --json` read: a row whose `sessionId` is the logged id about to be resumed refuses, `--fork` skips it, a failed read passes, its `agents-probe` pair in `run-<name>.ndjson`; `already-live` or `stale-heartbeat` → `no-session` → `session-live` → `cwd-missing`, each one `human::refuse` pair and one `process-exit{exit_code:1}` in `run-<name>.ndjson`), then program `claude` by name on its own `PATH`, child arguments `--plugin-dir <dir>`, `--resume <id>`, `--fork-session` with `--fork`, then the words after `--`, spawned in the snapshot's recorded `cwd`, the folder its start's trust record is keyed by. It logs as process `run`, replays no launch, keeps the parent and role its real snapshot records, and its first record is `wheel{driver, start}`. `--list` prints `<ts>  <cause>  <id>` per logged session; under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`, once its strict-modes check passed, it writes `process-start` and `process-exit{subject:"self"}` (`exit_code` 0, or 1 `detail:"no-session"` on an empty chain) into the caller's `cli-<VIOLA_NAME>.ndjson`, and with no name opens none. Both arms take `--json` (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-machine-contract): every refusal of its start, a refused strict-modes check and a preflight refusal among them, prints `{"v":1,"error":"<code>","detail":null}` (`strict-modes-failed` · `already-live` · `no-session` · `session-live` · `cwd-missing` · `stale-heartbeat` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `squatted-name` · `socket-dir-refused` · `internal-error`, a `claude` not on `PATH` or an anyhow error of the start being `internal-error`; `client::refused_document`) on stdout in place of its pair where it has one, stderr empty, the same exit 1 and the same log lines; `--list --json` prints `{"v":1,"ok":{"sessions":[…]}}` in log order, or the `no-session` document with exit 1; `Launch` carries `json: bool` (`run` false, `revive` `args.json`), and with it true `refused_with` (`src/cmd/run.rs`) prints the document in place of the human pair before `spawn_child`; a `pump_child` error prints no document, because the child has held the terminal.

- **List verb:** `src/cmd/list.rs` (`viola list [--json]`: caller-side, no channel frame and no wrapper contacted; `viola_state::board::scan` — the strict-modes check of the home, `instances/` and each instance before any log, whose refusal refuses the whole board with exit 21 and no log — then `board::read`, then one `claude agents --json` read (`run::agents::read_here`, `claude` resolved by `run::resolve_program` from its current directory) joined by `viola_state::board::join` (a row matching a wrapped item's `child_pid` or `agent_session_id` sets its `status` to `idle` or `busy`; every unjoined row is a read-only unwrapped item; a failed, oversize or malformed read leaves every `status` `unknown` and no unwrapped item); the `--json` `{items, links?, skipped}` document or the human board as one stdout write (`write_board`: with a known terminal width the unwrapped NAME cut, at a colour depth from `src/human/style.rs` the spans); exits 0 / 21 / 1 / 2; `board_document` (scan → read → document) is the provider `viola mcp` hands `viola_mcp::serve` for the `list` tool, which returns the document's `ok`, or `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `strict-modes-failed` for the board's refusal, its only one, while CLI `list` keeps its own order: scan, its log opened, read, document); **Wait / last verbs:** `src/cmd/wait.rs`, `src/cmd/last.rs` over `src/cmd/client.rs` (`refuse_untrusted`, the instance strict-modes check (`check_instance` on the absolute home and `instances/<name>`) that every CLI frame verb (send, wait, last, answer, pause, release) and `link` / `unlink` run first (refused: exit 21 with the instance pair, or the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed` under `--json`; nothing opened under the home, no line); `connect`, the verified connection every CLI frame verb (send, wait, last, answer, pause, release, link, unlink) opens: the live endpoint (`viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint` → `LiveEndpoint`, shared with `viola-mcp`'s frame tools), then `check_endpoint_dir` on it, then the client, then `peer_admitted(client.server_euid())`, then the server identity check; the closed `Unreachable` (`Dead` · `Unwrapped` · `Lost` · `ServerUnverified` · `SocketDir`, each an `UnreachableCause` through `cause()`; `answer_of` reads `Connect` as `Dead` and `Closed | Io` as `Lost`, a missing live endpoint reads `Unreachable::without_endpoint`, so a stale instance reads `instance-dead`; `hint_cause` keys the human hint) and `CallError`; `unreachable_document`, the one writer of the exit-21 document, `{"v":1,"error":"instance-unreachable","detail":"<cause>"}`, `<cause>` one of `strict-modes-failed` · `instance-dead` · `unwrapped-name` · `endpoint-lost` · `server-verify-failed` · `socket-dir-refused`; the channel client those verbs share, the `cli` obs start, the reply shapes (a `wrapper-fault`'s `message` a fixed text and `data` a closed object or null, read through `viola_channel::sanitised_fault`; a fault code outside the five the fixed `wrapper fault`, its human line `error: wrapper fault  <code>`; a `refusal` that is no code word read as `unknown`, a string `detail` that is no code word as `null`, a non-string `detail` as no known reply), exit 20 / exit 21 — the latter at WARN with `detail:"instance-dead"` + `during:"connect"`, or `detail:"server-verify-failed"` + `during:"connect"` and no `channel-request` line for a failed server check, a server of another euid included, or `detail:"socket-dir-refused"` + `during:"connect"` and no `channel-request` line for a refused socket directory; exit 21 also with `detail:"unwrapped-name"` + `during:"connect"`, or `detail:"endpoint-lost"` + `during:"call"` for a wrapper lost with the call open); human lines in `src/human/wait.rs` and the message-mode escaper in `src/human/escape.rs`; **MCP verb:** `src/cmd/mcp.rs` (the hidden `viola mcp`, `#[command(hide = true)]`, no argument but the global `--home`: its home and `diagnostics/` (each that exists) through `viola_state::strict::check_path` before anything opens, exit 1 with nothing on stdout or stderr and no role file on a refusal; then `viola_mcp::serve`, the five tools over stdio until stdin closes or a stdin line passes `MAX_FRAME`, which ends the session as a close does: exit 0 once initialized, 1 before `initialize`, both streams empty); **Plugin verb:** `src/cmd/plugin.rs` (`viola plugin install [--json]`: `check_path` on the home and the four `marketplace/` tree dirs before any write or log, exit 21 on a refusal (the home-state pair, or under `--json` the `instance-unreachable` document with `detail` `strict-modes-failed` through `client::unreachable_document`; nothing created, no log opened); then the `marketplace/` tree (dirs 0700 through `create_private_dir`, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, `viola/.claude-plugin/plugin.json` and `viola/.mcp.json` 0600 through `replace_private`, rewritten whole on every run, the documents from `viola_agent_claude::marketplace::marketplace_files`, no `claude` spawned), the `{"v":1,"ok":{"marketplace":"viola","plugin":"viola@viola"}}` document or the two printed commands (`write_plugin_installed` in `src/human/verbs.rs`); exits 0 / 21 / 1 / 2)

- Normalised kinds live only in `viola-core`, never with Claude-specific names: `session-start`, `turn-ended` `{last_assistant_message, background_tasks, scheduled_wakes, cause?}` (`cause` present only on an API-error turn end, one word of the closed nine-word `TurnEndCause` set: `rate-limited`, `overloaded`, `auth-failed`, `billing`, `invalid-request`, `model-not-found`, `server-error`, `output-limit`, `api-error`; absent on a Stop end), `prompt-submitted`, `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `session-end`, `activity`, `link`, `unlink`, `wheel`, `send-issued` `{cursor, from?}`, `send-confirmed` `{cursor, confirmed?}` (`confirmed:false` only for an unconfirmable send), `send-refused` `{refusal, detail, cursor?}` (the CL-1 send records, `source: wrapper`; `cursor` absent for a refusal before `send-issued`), `dialog-expired` `{dialog_id, dialog_kind}` (`source: wrapper`, appended once when a held dialog's hold ends; it carries no question, plan or tool text), `lineage` `{parent, role}` (each a string or `null`, `source: wrapper`).

- `wait` wakes only on `turn-ended`, `question`, `permission`, `plan`, `session-end`, `dialog-expired` (the one wrapper-appended kind that wakes it, appended through `WaitFeed::appending`); `activity`, `link`, `unlink`, `wheel`, `lineage`, a harness-origin `prompt-submitted` and the send records are log-only. The wake is by event kind alone: every `turn-ended` wakes whatever its `background_tasks` or `scheduled_wakes`, and telling a finished turn from a paused one is the driver's.

- An unsupported `v` or a parse failure → ignore the snapshot and replay the log; replay recovers only `links`, `agent_session_id`, `wheel`, `lineage` (`dialog_pending` reads false; the last `lineage` line replaces the held value). The wrapper appends no budget-gate line and the snapshot holds no budget field. As landed the classified read and the replay are library code (`viola_state::snapshot::read_snapshot_classified`, `viola_state::replay`) with product readers, each after the instance's strict-modes check has passed: `viola revive`'s preflight (one read for both its collision check and its recorded directory), `viola list`'s `viola_state::board::read` (a replayed snapshot gives a `live` row only for a beat at most `STALE_AFTER` old, never `stale`), `viola_state::liveness::live_endpoint` (the CLI frame verbs, `viola link` / `viola unlink` and `viola mcp`'s frame tools; only a real snapshot gives an endpoint), `viola hook`'s `connect` (a replayed or absent snapshot is unreachable, so the hook fails open) and `run`'s collision check (a replayed snapshot judged by the heartbeat alone: `already-live` within `STALE_AFTER`, else free); no product code under `src/` calls `read_snapshot`. The replay writes no file but logs one `state-recovered` line (an absent snapshot is neither replayed nor logged), gives no `cwd` (a revive over a replayed snapshot is refused `cwd-missing`), and recovers `links` from the logged `link` / `unlink` lines in its one pass through `replay::apply_link_line` (a `link` line with no string `ts` reads `since: "unknown"`). `replay::session_chain` reads the logged session ids in one pass and logs nothing.

- Colour decision order (first match → no colour): `--json` · `viola run` · `viola hook`/`mcp` · `NO_COLOR` (present, an empty value included) · `TERM=dumb` · non-TTY stdout. SGR only for amber `DIALOG`, dim `stale` rows, bold NAME — always beside its word; never on `unable` / `fail`. As built (chunk 2026-10-17-cli-output-discipline), `list` is uncoloured under any rung above; on a terminal that takes colour every NAME value is bold, the `DIALOG` word of a wrapped row with a pending dialog takes the attention token (its kind word plain), a wrapped `stale` row is dim from its first byte to its last (NAME dim and bold; on a stale row with a dialog only `DIALOG` amber and not dim), the BAY line, caption, empty-board line and separator carry no SGR, and after the board and the unwrapped rack a `-- LINKS --` block prints one `<driver> -> <driven>` line per link, sorted, deduplicated and name-checked, with no SGR, absent when there is no link, the spans are laid over the escaped, padded cells (the plain board's columns, one write), and the depth is truecolor / 256 / 16 from `COLORTERM` / `TERM` (`COLUMNS`, `CLICOLOR`, `CLICOLOR_FORCE` and `CI` are not read). A wrapped row joined to one `claude agents --json` read by child pid or agent session id reads STATUS `idle` or `busy`, else `unknown`; each unjoined session follows under the `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` line, sorted by name, NAME its `sessionId`, LIVE `live`, its STATUS, `n/a` in WHEEL, DIALOG and CLI, with no separator when there is none and the board as with no `claude` on a failed read. With the terminal's width known (`viola_pty::host_size()`, never `COLUMNS`) only an unwrapped NAME longer than its column (capped at the width less 65) is cut, to the column less 3 characters plus `...`, never inside an escape; wrapped rows are drawn as a tree, each child under its parent with its NAME cell indented two spaces per depth (the indent counted in NAME's column width), and a wrapped NAME is never cut, and a piped board or `--json` keeps every name whole.

- Methods: `send`, `wait`, `last`, `answer`, `pause`, `release`, `link`, `unlink`, `hook.dialog` (requests, integer ids monotonic per connection); `hook.event` (notification, `{ts, event:{kind, data}, transcript?}`: the optional string `transcript` beside `event`, never inside it, sent only for a SessionStart whose transcript path passes the shape check against its own session id, re-validated by the wrapper for a session-start line only, any other dropped, never entering event data). `link` `{driver, driven}` → `{since, already_linked}` (a held pair appends nothing and answers its `since` with `already_linked: true`) and `unlink` `{driver, driven}` → `{}` (an absent pair appends nothing), each sent to the driven instance's wrapper, reading no `from` and answered only after its event line and the snapshot write; a missing, non-string or invalid name, a `driven` that is not the wrapper's own name and a `driver` equal to `driven` are each `-32602` with `data: null`, no line written, and a failed record or remove is `-32603`. A `send` or an `answer` whose `from` is another instance's name records the implicit link (before `send-issued`; before the answer is taken), and a link that cannot be recorded answers `-32603` with nothing issued or the answer not taken. `list` is not a channel method — it reads the disk (and, by contract, `claude agents --json`) caller-side and needs no live wrapper; its `ok` payload is `{items, links?, skipped}` in the shapes of the `list` payload (Standard Contracts), returned whole, with `skipped{unknown_kinds,unknown_fields,torn_lines}`. As landed CLI `list` reads `<home>/instances/`, then makes one `claude agents --json` read joined by `viola_state::board::join`: a row matching a wrapped item's `child_pid` or `agent_session_id` sets that item's `status` to `idle` or `busy`, and every unjoined row is an unwrapped item (`wrapped: false`, its name the row's `sessionId`, never a `ViolaName` or a valid `target`); a failed, oversize or malformed read leaves every `status` `unknown` and no unwrapped item. `mcp`'s `list` tool (chunk 2026-10-17-mcp-server-for-drivers) builds the same board through `list::board_document` (scan → read with the one `claude agents --json` read and join → document, run on a blocking thread, its `agents-probe` pair in `diagnostics/mcp.ndjson`) on each call and returns the document's `ok`, or `instance-unreachable` with `detail` `strict-modes-failed` for the board's refusal, its only one.

- Exit codes: 0 ok · 1 internal / a `run` start refusal (its refused home-tree check before the wrapper log included: the home or the instance pair, no log, no child; its refused socket directory too, `socket_dir_ready` before any snapshot, child or `Server::bind`: the `unable:` / `hint:` pair, or under `viola revive --json` the `socket-dir-refused` document, and one `process-exit{subject:"self", exit_code:1, detail:"socket-dir-refused"}`, no path, pid or uid, a failed create reading the same code and a `Server::bind` failure not), a `revive` strict-modes, home-tree, preflight, socket-directory or start refusal, a `verify` failing row, refusal (its refused home-tree check of the home, `ledger/`, `bin/` and `plugin/` before its `cli` log, and `update_stamps`'s `StampsError::StrictModes`, each the home-state pair, included; a refused home tree writes no line, a failing row carries no code, and every other refusal carries its `Ended::Refused` code, `program-not-found` · `pinned-hash-mismatch` · `version-unreadable` · `strict-modes-failed` · `unclean-fixture`, beside `interrupted`, on the `process-exit` it writes under a parsed `VIOLA_NAME`; `verify` takes no `--json`) or Ctrl-C / TERM stop (no stamp written, `unable: verify was stopped before it finished`), `list`'s `instances/` that cannot be listed or failed log start, the hidden `viola mcp`'s home or `diagnostics/` (each that exists) failing `viola_state::strict::check_path` (nothing on stdout or stderr, no role file) or a stdin line past `MAX_FRAME` before `initialize` (both streams empty, one `parse-rejected{mcp-stdin, oversize, count:1}` line;
